findings.issue: AC-1, AC-7, AC-8, AC-9, AC-10, AC-12, AC-13, AC-14 are all marked 'verifiable_as: test' in the spec contract but have no behavioral test coverage. The test file explicitly acknowledges the gap ('Tests that require live Postgres (AC-1, 7, 8, 9, 10) are not included here — they rely on the route handlers exercised in integration') but no ci/checks/db/secret-handle.test.ts exists. AC-12/13/14 are covered only by static source-file grep (confirms audit type constants exist in the module, but does not assert an audit_event row is written to the DB). The codebase pattern is clear: T-0030 has ci/checks/db/grant-editor.test.ts covering its analogous DB-backed ACs (AC-01/07/12/13 etc.). T-0025 has no equivalent. Spec says 'test'; zero behavioral route-level tests exist.
findings.suggestion: Add ci/checks/db/secret-handle.test.ts (run via npm run fitness:db, requires DATABASE_URL) covering: AC-1 (POST sets column, DB read confirms non-NULL), AC-7 (PUT atomically overwrites), AC-8 (DELETE sets NULL, GET status returns {bound:false}), AC-9 (GET status returns {bound:true, summary:...} without the full handle in body), AC-10 (cross-tenant write returns 404, target tenant row unchanged), AC-12/13/14 (query audit_event after each mutating op, assert correct type + no handle in payload). Use the pattern from ci/checks/db/grant-editor.test.ts (createServer() + fetch against test port + real DB).

findings.issue: AC-11 test covers validator isolation only (validateSecretHandleShape and redactHandle do not call console.*). This is the pure-function path. The AC spec says 'Every setSecretHandle call (success AND rejection) produces NO log line containing the submitted handle value'. The HTTP route handler (handleSetSecretHandle) receives handleValue and passes it to SQL. If a future debug log is added to the route handler, this test would not catch it. The static FF-25-4 grep catches console.* calls, which is a good backstop — but the behavioral route-level test (R-1 above) is where a real runtime check would land.
findings.suggestion: In the DB-backed test suite (R-1), capture stdout/stderr around the HTTP call and assert the handle value does not appear in captured output (matching the full AC-11 spec intent, not just the validator half).

findings.issue: ORG_SEED_CHILDREN is re-declared in secret-handle.ts (lines 54-62). The identical seed oracle also exists in grants.ts. Two copies of the same hard-coded org tree means any future seed change requires two edits. This is acknowledged as 'duplication by precedent' in the ADR (write-path own transaction), but the SEED_ORACLE is not a transaction primitive — it is a business-fixture constant. A future T-0053 DAO extraction could unify them; not blocking now but worth tracking.
findings.suggestion: Track as a cleanup candidate when T-0053 (DAO extraction) lands. No change required for this task.
